papers.abstract: Robots manipulating in cluttered spaces must often plan from partial views where foreground objects occlude the target, surrounding geometry, and usable free space. Reactive policies often miss these hidden constraints, while exhaustive search becomes computationally prohibitive in dense clutter. We present SCOUT, an occlusion-aware planning framework that bridges high-level deliberation with grounded physical rollouts. SCOUT leverages an object-centric scene representation to reconstruct hidden geometry and derive a relational planning state capturing blocker hierarchies and accessibility corridors. To navigate the vast action space in clutter, an LLM proposes structured action candidates which are then rigorously evaluated via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) using a learned action-conditioned world model. Evaluations on 'Reveal' and 'Placement' tasks show that SCOUT outperforms Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, embodied agents, and 3D world models, with significant gains in long-horizon tasks requiring reasoning over occluded geometry. We further validate the framework's robustness through real-world robotic manipulation in a cluttered shelf environment.

papers.title: Cutoff and a Gaussian-shift profile for the Rudvalis shuffle
papers.authors: Yunjiang Jiang
papers.abstract: The Rudvalis shuffle removes the top card and reinserts it uniformly at random in one of the bottom two positions. Hildebrand proved the classical upper bound $O(n^3\log n)$, and Wilson later proved the sharp lower coefficient $1/(8π^2)$, establishing the correct order but leaving the leading upper constant, cutoff, and the cutoff profile open. We prove that the full labelled shuffle has total-variation cutoff at \[   \frac{n^3\log n}{8π^2} \] with a window of order $n^3$.   The upper bound is obtained by writing one deterministic rotation of the shuffle as a nonnormal sweep of adjacent averaging projections, comparing that sweep to a weighted interchange generator, and controlling the entire regular-representation heat trace. The key sharp-window ingredients are heat-kernel smoothing through the Octopus Inequality, zero extension of deletion-harmonic ordered-tuple functions, a representation-theoretic multiplicity payment, and a sectorwise entrance estimate that disposes of all large Young-diagram deficits. For the profile, an exact complex one-card eigenfunction yields a deck statistic whose surviving first Fourier mode converges to a Gaussian shift. A matching full-deck $L^2$ bound then shows that this one-dimensional Gaussian likelihood ratio asymptotically exhausts all remaining information, giving the exact total-variation profile.

papers.title: Smoothed analysis of stability radii for the assignment problem
papers.authors: Michael P. Friedlander
papers.abstract: Every linear program can tolerate small changes to its costs and still yield a solution of the original problem. The size of this tolerance measures how robust an optimal decision is to noise or numerical error, and how much regularization the problem can support. Classical sensitivity analysis can determine this tolerance only from an optimal solution. This paper provides a priori lower bounds on two measures of this tolerance -- the optimality gap and the $\infty$-norm stability radius -- for the $n$-by-$n$ linear assignment problem over the Birkhoff polytope. The bounds derive from a smoothed analysis, which adds Gaussian noise with standard deviation of at least $σ$ in every direction to an arbitrary base cost. At every fixed confidence level, uniformly over the base cost, both quantities are at least of order $σ/(n\sqrt{\log n})$. The radius bound is asymptotically sharp. Under isotropic noise, the worst case occurs when every assignment has equal cost, and in this case, a scaled stability radius converges in distribution to a standard exponential variable.

papers.title: Second-Order Asymptotics for the Scalar Gaussian Broadcast Channel
papers.authors: Vincent Y. F. Tan
papers.abstract: This paper characterizes the second-order coding region of the scalar Gaussian broadcast channel along the curved boundary of its capacity region. The characterization holds under both average and maximal error criteria and allows correlation between the receiver noises. At each interior point of this boundary, the second-order region is a halfspace, as in the work of Scarlett and the author on Gaussian multiple-access channels with degraded message sets. Achievability follows from spherical superposition coding with a blocklength-dependent power allocation. The main innovation lies in the converse. Using Ornstein--Uhlenbeck entropy dissipation and Gaussian functional inequalities, we construct an auxiliary observation through an additive Gaussian noise channel and establish quantitative relative entropy bounds for the channel output distributions conditioned on this observation. The strong functional representation lemma of Li and El Gamal then allows us to select a realization of its independent random seed to obtain a deterministic partition of the retained receiver-1 message set. The component label plays a role analogous to the auxiliary random variable in the capacity characterization, while providing the distributional control needed at the second-order scale. These properties guide the construction of auxiliary output measures whose likelihood ratios admit the cancellations and normal approximation needed to evaluate an information spectrum converse.

papers.title: Exact solution of the dynamic pseudogap model: Fock-space formalism for Gaussian fluctuations
papers.authors: Michael V. Sadovskii
papers.abstract: We present an exact solution of the dynamic finite-$Q$ pseudogap model, in which electrons scatter between two nested Fermi-surface patches off a classical Gaussian order-parameter field with characteristic frequency $ω_0$ and damping $γ$. The disorder-averaged Green's function is shown to be a single matrix element of the resolvent of a sparse non-Hermitian matrix acting on a Fock space of two (commensurate fluctuations) or four (incommensurate fluctuations) bosonic modes with complex energies. The non-commutativity of the pseudospin vertices at different times, which prevented an exact treatment so far, is retained in full. We derive the representation, its symmetries, and the exact limits it contains: the static continued fractions, the closed-form commensurate solution at the Fermi surface, and the second-order self-energy. A numerically exact implementation gives spectral functions and densities of states for all values of the fluctuation frequency, damping and electron energy. We find that the sideband comb of the spectral function stays close to multiples of $ω_0$ and that quasiparticle damping is governed by an energy-dependent decoherence rate. At resonance of a quasiparticle energy with $ω_0/2$, we obtain the static fuctuating-gap in a rotating frame, which leads to resonant splitting of the quasiparticle peak.

papers.title: Detecting Generated-Depth Injection Attacks on RGB-D Place Authentication
papers.authors: Seigo Kawachi; Satoshi Matsuura
papers.abstract: Advances in monocular depth estimation (MDE) now let an attacker generate depth from publicly available RGB images and submit forged RGB-D queries. Such attacks break a core assumption of RGB-D place authentication: that depth comes from a sensor. We study a presentation attack detection (PAD) classifier that uses geometric consistency between the enrollment and query views, as a software-layer defense. A three-stage evaluation shows how far this classifier detects software-injected depth, depending on how accurately the attacker knows the camera intrinsics. In the first stage, the attacker has only an estimate of the intrinsics, and the PAD classifier separates forgeries generated by all three MDE models with a validation area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.997-0.999. In the second stage, the attacker obtains the exact intrinsics, and the original PAD classifier falls to near chance (AUC 0.54-0.61); a retrained PAD classifier, however, still has the registration residual between enrollment and query as a cue. In the third stage, an oracle evaluation, in which the evaluator fits warps using the ground-truth 3D geometry, shows that detection falls to near chance only in its strongest case, where every valid query keypoint is given its ground-truth 3D coordinate. Of the detection cues, the reprojection error captures the attacker's misestimate of the intrinsics, whereas the registration residual remains even when the attacker knows the exact intrinsics.

papers.title: Rank-Optimal Sample Complexity of Riemannian Gauss-Newton for Low-Rank Matrix Recovery
papers.authors: Xunmeng Wu; Jian-Feng Cai; Zongben Xu; Zai Yang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the recovery of an unknown rank-$r$ matrix $\boldsymbol{X}_\star \in \mathbb{R}^{n_1\times n_2}$ from Gaussian linear measurements using the Riemannian Gauss-Newton (RGN) algorithm. Each iteration of RGN solves the RGN equation followed by a fixed-rank retraction. We prove that, with high probability, RGN with spectral initialization converges quadratically to $\boldsymbol{X}_\star$ using $\mathcal{O} ( r(n_1+n_2)κ^2 )$ measurements, where $κ$ is the condition number of $\boldsymbol{X}_\star$. This is the first result to simultaneously achieve rank-optimal sample complexity and quadratic convergence for Gaussian low-rank matrix sensing. The key to the proof is a sharp spectral-norm analysis of the iterates, which requires controlling the inverse operator arising from the RGN equation. Our analysis develops an exact finite Neumann expansion of this inverse operator and combines it with a virtual-sequence decoupling argument and the restricted isometry property. Extensive numerical experiments support our theoretical findings and demonstrate the advantages of RGN.

papers.title: MoPort: A View-Aware 2D Interface for Motion Language Models
papers.authors: Lixing Tan; Qing Xia; Yuting Guo; Shuai Li; Aimin Hao
papers.abstract: Motion language models (MoLMs) encode 3D human motion as discrete tokens for language-based understanding. Deploying them on monocular video raises two problems. Pose detection yields 2D joint sequences, leaving a dimensional gap from the 3D motion used in training. Moreover, the 2D observation changes with the camera viewpoint, while the depth lost in projection makes the 2D pose ambiguous across viewpoints. We propose MoPort, a view-aware 2D interface that enables MoLMs to take 2D observations as input. We introduce Paired View Alignment (PVA), which gives two views of the same motion a shared 3D teacher target and directly constrains the consistency of their latents, so that 2D observations from different viewpoints are mapped to a consistent semantic representation. Camera-Modulated Encoding (CME) estimates the camera extrinsics from the 2D sequence and uses them to modulate encoding, providing the 2D latents with geometric information about the viewpoint. MoPort achieves R@1 of 0.5674 on HumanML3D and 0.3286 on KIT-ML, outperforming all evaluated baselines. On HumanML3D, its R@1 decreases only from 0.5763 on in-distribution viewpoints to 0.5585 on out-of-distribution viewpoints. We validate portability on three downstream MoLMs. Furthermore, on the real-world RGB video dataset Fit3D, MoPort achieves 80.36\% accuracy. Code will be released upon acceptance.

papers.title: Task-driven sparse-view planar X-ray computed tomography for axial metrology
papers.authors: Yibin Tian; Shuming Yang; Wolfgang Heidrich
papers.abstract: Computational imaging can reduce the acquisition burden when the system is designed around task-relevant information rather than complete image recovery. We investigate this framework for sparse-view planar X-ray tomography (XCT) of layered objects, using measurement of the axial termination gap (ATG) of back-drilled printed-circuit-board (PCB) vias as a representative task. Instead of using 3D reconstruction, the proposed method estimates ATG directly from polychromatic projection data through a physics-based sensitivity model. A gated hierarchical estimator first fits ATG together with radiometric perturbations and selectively introduces global geometry and specimen-warp models only when a reduced chi-squared adequacy test and Bayesian information criterion justify the added degrees of freedom. The same low-dimensional perturbation model is incorporated into marginalized Fisher-information analyses, yielding task-specific conditional and calibration-aware Cram'er-Rao bounds. Numerical experiments show that, under a fixed total photon budget, task-driven metrology changes little over 12-64 views, while reconstruction-driven metrology is strongly view-dependent with much larger errors. The direct estimator also follows the expected photon-limited scaling. These results demonstrate a computational sensing strategy in which XCT acquisition, physical modeling, and inference are evaluated according to the quantitative information required by the task rather than for general-purpose volumetric image fidelity.

papers.title: Covariance-dependent participation scaling of Comtet disorder on open hyperbolic lattices
papers.authors: Wei Li; Yong Cheng
papers.abstract: Negative curvature makes the electrostatic Green function decay exponentially, producing a finite disorder-variance budget even as radial volume grows exponentially. We investigate whether this near-field concentration also determines wave-function participation on open hyperbolic lattices. A Gaussian control preserves the full one-site distribution of Comtet disorder at every vertex while removing its off-diagonal covariance. Complete-window participation ratios on $\{7,3\}$ graphs with $N=847,2240,5887$ yield an effective-exponent difference of $-0.028$ at $W/t=0.5$ and $+0.116$ at $W/t=3$; both signs persist upon extending to $N=15435$. Size-resolved squared-kernel radii lie near $2.45\ell$ on the larger graphs of this sequence, below the cutoff-matched continuum value $3.12\ell$. Distance-shell weights resolve the finite discrete measure associated with this shift, while higher participation moments and spacing ratios characterize the accompanying wave-function and spectral structure. A marginal-matched exponential-kernel family gives positive exponent contrasts at all five sampled kernel lengths at $W/t=0.5,3$, separating the Comtet response from a description based on the decay length alone. These results distinguish a concentrated variance budget from the covariance-dependent participation response of finite open hyperbolic systems.

papers.title: ContactCut: A Partition-Aware Contact Selection Framework for False-Merge Correction in Connectomics
papers.authors: Byunghyun Ko; Won-Ki Jeong; Chaoli Wang
papers.abstract: Localized false-merge correction in connectomics requires converting an identified error into an executable native 3D partition. Still, neither intermediate correction predictions nor seeded graph solvers alone determine which native source-sink constraints should define that partition. We formulate this problem as a 3D-native partition-aware contact selection problem: selecting candidate contacts based on the complete partitions they induce. Our solution comprises two components: ContactCut (CC)-Auto, which uses learned single-contact selection, and ContactCut (CC)-Search, which enables bounded paired-contact search, generates compact alternatives, and applies learned panel ranking. On historical two-way false-merge corrections from MICrONS and FlyWire, CC-Auto improves failure-aware 3D partition (FA-3D Part.) mIoU by 5.9 and 3.4 points over the strongest graph-based controls and by 12.5 and 10.0 points over the best learned baselines. A MICrONS-trained ranker transfers to FlyWire with negligible degradation. CC-Search expands oracle reachability and prioritizes near-oracle alternatives. The code is available at https://github.com/bentake/ContactCut.

papers.title: An Odd-Arch Family of Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursions: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws
papers.authors: Marco Mantovanelli
papers.abstract: For every integer $p\ge2$, we construct a globally well-defined positive odd sequence $Q_p$ satisfying, after an explicit finite initial block, $Q_p(n)=Q_p(n-Q_p(n-1))+Q_p(n-Q_p(n-2))-(-1)^n$.   Its binary block words admit the exact factorization $U_{p,k}=(A_k\overline{A}_{k+1})^{p-1}A_{k+2}$, producing exactly $2p-1$ alternating signed arches per natural block. The elementary word heights converge uniformly to the Gaussian isoperimetric profile $\varphi\circΦ^{-1}$.   For each fixed $p$, this yields an explicit dyadic limiting profile with $2p-1$ sign transitions and a sharp relative-error constant $Λ_p=b_p/2$, where $b_p$ is determined by $b_p((3p-1)/2+Φ(-b_p))=\varphi(b_p)$.   We determine all zeros and parity crossings in sufficiently large dyadic blocks. For $p\ge3$, there are exactly $2p-1$ transverse even-index zeros, whereas the three-arch case $p=2$ exhibits an alternating four/six-zero pattern.   An ordered frequency factorization gives exact dyadic histograms, moments, total-variation distances, and extremal multiplicities. The limiting frequency generating function $z^3/(2-z)$ is universal, although the highest finite multiplicities depend on $p$.   Finally, the summatory function has main terms $N^2/4+(N/2)\log_2N$, an explicit parameter-dependent log-periodic term of order $N$, and remainder $O_p(N/\sqrt{\log N})$.

papers.title: Correctness and Predictive Uncertainty in Bayesian TSK Fuzzy Regression: A Reproducible Evaluation on Tabular and Building-Meter Data
papers.authors: Zhiren Xiao
papers.abstract: Uncertainty estimates from fuzzy regression are informative only when the implementation is correct and the comparison protocol makes the sources of variation visible. We revisit a first-order Takagi--Sugeno--Kang (TSK) regression implementation and rebuild its dense, conjugate Bayesian, BIC-based, and rule-level spike-and-slab estimators using corrected code. The corrected pipeline freezes the Gaussian membership partition at training time, uses a scaled conjugate prior, evaluates firing strengths in the log domain, and reports direct posterior-predictive quantiles for Bayesian methods. Across 30 outer 80/20 splits on three targets from two UCI regression datasets, corrected TSK-LS obtains $R^2=0.957$, $0.923$, and $0.786$ on Energy-Heating, Energy-Cooling, and Concrete, respectively; rule-level Gibbs sampling with Bayesian model averaging obtains $0.957$, $0.922$, and $0.784$. We then evaluate the same workflow on a bounded chronological sample of the Building Data Genome 2 meter data that covers 158 buildings across 17 sites. In a common-unit evaluation, every method is scored on the same 47,400 test rows and every trained model uses 94,800 train--validation rows. Persistence has RMSE $27.710$, compared with $29.083$ for both TSK-LS and Bayesian TSK; the pre-specified building-level mean RMSE difference between Bayesian TSK and persistence is $+0.0447$ with a 95% site-cluster bootstrap interval of $[-1.5536,1.5665]$. The Bayesian TSK 90% intervals have PICP $0.980$ and MPIW $116.469$. Taken together, the evidence supports a narrower conclusion: spike-and-slab model averaging is a reproducible implementation option, but it does not provide a demonstrated accuracy or calibration advantage across the tested tabular and building-meter settings.

papers.title: $p$-Wasserstein distance and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk
papers.authors: Shuyuan Liang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish $p$-Wasserstein bounds and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk in the diffusive and critical regimes. Using a Gaussian convolution estimate with random covariance and the recursions for the conditional covariance, we obtain $W_{p,2}(\mathcal L(\widehat T_n),N(0,I_d))\le C_{a,d}pL_n$, where $\widehat T_n$ is normalized by its exact covariance and \[ L_n\asymp \begin{cases} n^{-1/2}\log n,&a\le1/3,\\ n^{-3(1/2-a)},&1/3<a<1/2,\\ (\log n)^{-3/2},&a=1/2. \end{cases} \] Consequently, we obtain radial Cramér-type moderate deviations for $x=o(L_n^{-1/3})$. We also determine the covariance bias under the uncorrected normalization and establish the corresponding Wasserstein bounds, lower bounds and moderate deviation estimates. The dimension and the model parameters are fixed.

papers.title: Boson sampling is fragile to loss
papers.authors: Youngrong Lim
papers.abstract: Boson sampling experiments aim to demonstrate quantum computational advantage with increasing numbers of interfering photons. A central question is whether their computational hardness survives under photon loss. We show that even an arbitrarily small nonzero uniform loss rate permits efficient classical sampling in the average case when the rate remains fixed as the system grows. We exploit how loss suppresses correlations involving many photons to approximate the full output distribution using low correlation orders. The resulting samplers run in time polynomial in system size and inverse total variation error, with the error averaged over Haar random interferometers. The results apply to Fock state boson sampling with single-photon states in distinct input modes and arbitrary additional vacuum inputs, and to Gaussian boson sampling with equal squeezing of bounded strength in every input mode. Classical sampling is efficient even when the mean detected photon number grows linearly with system size, showing that large photon counts alone do not ensure computational hardness.

papers.title: From Radiotherapy Dataset to Cherenkov Dose Map: A Digital Linac Monte Carlo Simulation Pipeline
papers.authors: Xianghuan He; Changyu Sun; Andy N. Wiles; Yao Hao; Gregory B. Biedermann et al.
papers.abstract: Background: Cherenkov-based radiotherapy monitoring depends on the relationship between dose and locally generated Cherenkov photons, before optical transport and detection. Purpose: To develop a DICOM RT-driven Geant4 digital linac Monte Carlo framework that scores dose and Cherenkov creation together and to evaluate their spatial correspondence. Methods: The framework converts DICOM CT, structure, plan, and dose objects into beam-delivery states and scores energy deposition and Cherenkov photon creation on a common 2.5-mm isotropic grid in a water-equivalent phantom. Static fields, different beam qualities, and a two-arc VMAT plan were tested. Monte Carlo dose was compared with TPS RTDOSE from Acuros XB and AAA; dose-Cherenkov associations and spatial agreement were assessed at voxel, plane, and profile levels. Results: Full-volume 3D dose gamma passing rates (3%/3 mm, 10% threshold) were 97.05%-98.86% for Acuros XB-referenced field-size and beam-quality cases (97.47% with AAA) and 97.84% for VMAT. Cherenkov creation correlated strongly with dose, with voxel $r^2 \geq 0.9890$ and projection/profile $r^2 \geq 0.9942$ in all cases. Dose-Cherenkov 3D gamma passing rates were 97.97%-99.16% for $10\times10$ 6X, 10X, and 15X fields and 96.59% for VMAT, but fell to 71.22% for $5\times5$ fields and 32.82% for 6FFF. Deviations were most apparent near small-field edges and along depth for 6FFF. Conclusions: In a homogeneous water phantom, local Cherenkov creation broadly tracks local dose but shows systematic differences at beam edges and with FFF beam quality. This framework supports future studies of optical transport and surface-based Cherenkov dosimetry.

papers.title: Log-Sobolev inequality for the sine-Gordon model in the subcritical regime
papers.authors: Alexandru F. Radu
papers.abstract: We prove a logarithmic Sobolev inequality for the massive two-dimensional sine-Gordon model throughout the subcritical range $0<β<8π$. For fixed mass, volume and arbitrary real coupling, the constant has a positive lower bound independent of the lattice spacing. When the dimensionless coupling is small, the lower bound is also uniform in volume and approaches the Gaussian constant as the coupling tends to zero. This extends the known range $β<6π$ and gives a rate of entropy decay for the reversible Langevin dynamics that remains positive as the cutoff is removed. The proof follows the Polchinski flow to a positive physical scale, where the Hamiltonian is a bounded perturbation of a uniformly convex one. For interactions invariant under constant field shifts, spatial differences bound their curvature by the gradient energy. For the oscillating part, we compare Gaussian integration with an average in which the original cosine phase fluctuates independently of the remaining variables. We estimate the comparison error at an intermediate scale, then differentiate the remaining Gaussian density. This preserves both phase damping and spatial decay without assuming bounds on second derivatives of the incoming local terms. The resulting strict gain between scales closes the estimates for every fixed $β<8π$.

papers.title: RadPose: ISAC-based RF 3D Human Pose Estimation
papers.authors: Geo Jie Zhou; Kunzhe Song; Ruxin Lin; Huacheng Zeng
papers.abstract: Human pose estimation under adverse lighting and occlusion conditions remains challenging for camera- and LiDAR-based systems. Although mmWave radars provide robustness to illumination and occlusion, they rely on dedicated hardware and licensed spectrum, limiting scalability. In this paper, we present RadPose, a learning-based monostatic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework that enables mmWave communication devices to perform 3D human pose estimation. Unlike specialized radars, RadPose leverages monostatic full-duplex operation to extract channel impulse responses (CIRs) directly from standard OFDM communication signals, generating 3D radio point clouds without additional sensing hardware. To address the sparsity and noise of RF observations, RadPose employs a cross-frame transformer-based pose inference network with semantic-guided spatial attention and target-driven temporal attention for robust spatio-temporal aggregation. It further adopts a joint-aware inverse kinematics refinement module based on graph convolution to enforce skeletal topology, bone-length consistency, and anatomical plausibility. Extensive experiments demonstrate RadPose achieves competitive accuracy compared to state-of-the-art radar-based approaches while maintaining robust performance in unseen and occluded scenarios. The dataset and source code are available at https://github.com/Geo-Chou/RadPose.

papers.title: SpecUltra: A Unified Foundation Model for Heterogeneous Spectral Images
papers.authors: Weili Kong; Baisen Liu; Xiaojun Bi; Jiaming Pei
papers.abstract: Spectral imagery, including hyperspectral image (HSI) and multispectral image (MSI), exhibits substantial heterogeneity in band numbers, wavelengths, spectral resolutions, hindering unified modeling and cross-sensor transfer. From the perspective of imaging physics, these heterogeneous observations can be regarded as discrete measurements of an underlying continuous spectrum acquired through different sampling processes. Motivated by this perspective, we propose SpecUltra, a unified foundation model for heterogeneous spectral images. Specifically, SpecUltra employs 3D convolutional tokenization and wavelength-aware 3D RoPE to encode relative wavelength and spatial relationships, enabling fine-grained spatial-spectral modeling within a shared coordinate system. We further construct MultiHyper-200K, a large-scale multi-sensor HSI dataset, and pretrain SpecUltra using auxiliary-token-assisted mask image modeling (MIM), where a level token indicates the radiometric product type and register tokens absorb sensor- and acquisition-dependent variations. To bridge the spectral-granularity gap between HSI and MSI, we introduce Spectral Kernel Transformation (SKT), which transfers pretrained knowledge in parameter space by constructing MSI embedding kernels from fine-grained HSI-pretrained kernel slices. This design preserves pretrained spectral priors while maintaining compatibility with the pretrained backbone. Experiments on HSI and MSI classification and segmentation benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art or competitive performance across disparate sensors and downstream tasks.

papers.title: Benign population landscapes do not transfer to empirical risk minimization in nonsmooth optimization
papers.authors: Penghao Wang; Mateo Díaz; Liwei Jiang
papers.abstract: Benign landscapes provide a geometric explanation for the success of iterative methods on nonconvex problems arising in data science. The landscape is benign if every local minimizer is global and every other critical point is a strict saddle. For methods that avoid strict saddles, convergence to a critical point therefore implies convergence to a global minimizer. For smooth stochastic optimization, a common strategy for establishing such landscapes proceeds in two steps: $(i)$ establish benign geometry for the population objective---which is often easier to analyze---and $(ii)$ transfer this geometry to the empirical objective using concentration of gradients and Hessians. Recent work has extended saddle-point avoidance guarantees to weakly convex nonsmooth optimization through the notion of active strict saddles. We show, however, that benign population geometry need not transfer to empirical objectives in this setting. Specifically, for robust phase retrieval with Gaussian measurements---a well-studied and highly structured problem---the population objective is benign. Nevertheless, the empirical objective has sharp spurious local minima with probability bounded away from zero as the sample size tends to infinity. This asymptotic probability lower bound is independent of the dimension.

papers.title: Mathematical modeling to study combination strategies for neural stem cell therapy in glioblastoma
papers.authors: Ashley Harrison; Austin Hansen; Anthony E. Bishay; Greg Grigoryan; Vikram Adhikarla et al.
papers.abstract: Neural stem cells (NSCs) are a promising treatment platform due to their ability to cross the restrictive blood-brain barrier and migrate toward damaged regions of the brain. These properties can be leveraged to target brain tumors, as NSCs can infiltrate tumor lesions and deliver therapeutic agents such as drugs, oncolytic viruses, and genetic materials. Despite the advantages of NSCs, translational challenges remain, including patient-specific chemotactic signaling and immune responses, variability in migration and localization at tumor sites, and optimization of delivery strategies. In this work, we focus on intranasal delivery of NSCs and combination strategies for the treatment of brain cancer. To investigate strategies for improving NSC arrival at the tumor site, we developed a hybrid mathematical model of NSC migration that couples an agent-based model with a partial differential equation, where cell motion is guided by the spatial dynamics of chemoattractants. Using data collected from a murine model and our mathematical model, we {investigate treatment-motivated downstream effects associated with three combination strategies:} (1) IL-10 pretreatment, (2) CXCL12 pretreatment, and (3) radiotherapy. We find that IL-10 pretreatment improves NSC arrival numbers at tumor only under the Gaussian chemoattractant profile, whereas CXCL12 pretreatment moderately improves arrival numbers when the tumor is located in the anterior brain. Radiotherapy significantly enhances the tumor arrival under uniform profiles. These simulation studies suggest that both treatment strategies and chemoattractant distribution influence intranasal NSC delivery, and the proposed model can be used to predict how targeted modulation of chemotactic signaling and tissue-guided migration may improve delivery outcomes.

papers.title: Minimax estimation of linear functionals in the Darcy inverse problem
papers.authors: Yi Liu; Xiaotian Chang; Qirui Hu
papers.abstract: We study estimation of linear functionals $\int fψ$ of the conductivity $f$ in the Darcy problem $\nabla\cdot(f\nabla u)=g$ from observations of $u$ in Gaussian white noise of level $N^{-1/2}$. When the potential has a single nondegenerate minimum, we determine the minimax rates over Sobolev balls in the linearised experiment. Unless a compatibility condition along the gradient flow holds, the rate is governed by an effective dimension $T$ of the Hessian at the minimum, not by the ambient dimension: it is $N^{-(2s+T)/(4s+8)}$ for $T<4$, has an elbow at $T=4$ with an extra logarithmic factor, and is parametric for $T>4$. In the nonlinear experiment we show that these lower bounds persist when compatibility fails at the reference and $T\le4$, and we prove the minimax rate on classes with isotropic critical Hessians, and the parametric rate near references with $T>4$. In dimension at most four, no nonzero linear functional is uniformly $\sqrt N$-estimable on a Sobolev neighbourhood of the constant conductivity, even when it is regular there.

papers.title: Likelihood-Free Schrödinger--Föllmer Sampling for Bayesian Inference with Fixed-Proposal Reuse
papers.authors: Xihan Ren; Zhijian He; Du Ouyang
papers.abstract: We study Bayesian posterior sampling when the likelihood is an expectation that is costly to evaluate. We construct a likelihood-free Schrödinger--Föllmer sampler whose drift is written as a ratio of expectations over Gaussian variables and simulator outputs and is estimated directly from joint draws of the two. Importance sampling with a fixed proposal allows the simulator outputs to be generated once and reused across all time steps and trajectories. For the likelihood-free Schrödinger--Föllmer sampler, which draws new Monte Carlo samples at each step, we bound the terminal Wasserstein error under regularity and moment assumptions, separating time-discretization and integration errors. For the likelihood-free Schrödinger--Föllmer sampler with sample reuse, we prove that the output converges to the posterior in the Wasserstein distance, assuming only a finite posterior second moment. Numerical experiments illustrate the reduction in simulator calls and the benefits of randomized quasi-Monte Carlo for drift estimation.

papers.title: Mixed-Integer Programming for Causal Discovery with Unknown Hard-Intervention Targets
papers.authors: Tong Xu; Armeen Taeb; Simge Küçükyavuz; Ali Shojaie
papers.abstract: When intervention targets are uncertain, learning causal relationships and identifying directly perturbed variables become a joint task. We develop an exact mixed-integer program based on optimized parent-set scores (PS-MIP) for joint graph and intervention-target estimation in linear Gaussian structural equation models under stochastic hard interventions. The method can incorporate candidate-edge restrictions and partial target knowledge when available. For each random variable, PS-MIP evaluates candidate sets of direct causes, or parent sets, by optimizing the likelihood parameters and compatible target patterns, retaining both the score and a minimizing target pattern. A global mixed-integer program then selects parent sets subject to acyclicity. Under stated conditions, this reduction preserves the joint objective and reconstructs the graph, targets, and likelihood parameters. Because the local scores are precomputed, PS-MIP replaces a direct large bilinear mixed-integer program with a linear selection problem; empirically it certifies global optimality on far more instances than the direct formulation (126 of 180 versus 34) and is often orders of magnitude faster. On synthetic data, PS-MIP achieves favorable false-discovery--true-discovery trade-offs relative to several benchmark algorithms for causal discovery with unknown intervention targets, along with strong intervention-target recovery in denser settings. An exploratory study on real data from a controlled physical system further demonstrates recovery beyond simulation.

papers.title: Does Random Search Discover Task Experts? Revisiting Neural Thickets
papers.authors: Julian Asilis; Guanzhe Hong; Vatsal Sharan
papers.abstract: Pretrained models are typically viewed as generalists, requiring bespoke post-training to achieve task-specific expertise. Gan & Isola (2026) recently proposed a striking alternative: that pretrained models lie in a dense neural thicket of task specialists, which can be surfaced with simple Gaussian weight perturbations. We examine this neural thicket of task-specific experts and identify several key findings that question this perspective. First, we find that the apparent lift of the best-of-N selected perturbation decays quickly with selection-set size m, strongly suggesting overfitting to the selection questions. In fact, for 10 of the 12 model-task pairs we study, a simple null model of pure selection noise predicts more than 75 percent of the top expert's reward lift. Second, the top experts' advantage often vanishes on held-out questions or remains within the run-to-run variability of the unperturbed pretrained model. Third, we find that majority voting over the top-K selected perturbations, termed RandOpt(N, K) by Gan & Isola (2026), is often matched or outperformed by majority voting over K samples from the base model. Overall, our results suggest that random weight perturbations may be ineffective at uncovering task experts around pretrained models, and that task adaptation requires more sophistication than random search. Code and artifacts are available at github.com/asil012/RevisitingNeuralThickets.

papers.title: Model-Based Co-Clustering for Censored Data
papers.authors: Kejun Fang; Mincen Liu; Qihuang Zhang
papers.abstract: Co-clustering jointly partitions the rows and columns of a data matrix. Standard co-clustering methods for continuous data typically assume that entries are observed exactly. Matrices with censored entries, such as assay measurements below a detection limit, are therefore commonly completed by substitution or imputation before co-clustering. Since the completed values are treated as exact, the estimated block means and partitions depend on the completion rule. We propose the censored Gaussian latent block model (CGLBM), in which each censored entry contributes the probability of its reported interval. We establish identifiability under a known Type I censoring design. Approximate standard errors for the block means follow from the Fisher information under censoring. CGLBM is fitted by a generalized expectation--maximization algorithm, and its row and column class numbers are selected by a BIC approximation to the integrated classification likelihood. In simulation studies, boundary substitution and truncated normal imputation attenuate the contrasts between block means, whereas the partition recovery of multiple imputation drops the most under heavy censoring. CGLBM preserves the contrasts, and its partition recovery drops the least. The method is implemented in the R package CGLBM.

papers.title: Learned Warm Starts for Steady Transonic RANS Simulations of Wing and Aircraft Configurations
papers.authors: Muhammad Irfan Zafar; Saleh Abuhanieh; Şahin Yiğit
papers.abstract: Neural surrogates can accelerate many-query aerodynamic analyses, but their standalone predictions may be insufficiently accurate or robust to support reliable design evaluations. We develop a learned warm-start formulation that predicts mean-flow and turbulence fields directly on native CFD meshes for subsequent correction by the RANS solver. A common architecture and objective structure are used across subcritical and transonic flows, including challenging conditions with shock-induced separation. A condition-modulated Transolver combines Fourier and wall features with target-gated regularization, a Sobolev-type loss, adaptive loss weighting and sampled training. Prediction requires no preliminary flow solution, and training requires no solver-residual evaluation. Extensive 3D CFD evaluations on SuperWing, the NASA Common Research Model (CRM) and DLR-F6 assess geometric and operating-condition generalization, including interpolation, extrapolation and cross-mesh deployment, using Spalart-Allmaras and $k$-$ω$ SST closures on million-cell meshes. Unseen nominal cases achieve geometric-mean iteration speed-ups of approximately $2$-$4\times$ under a common convergence criterion based on cold-run aerodynamic coefficients. On CRM, learned initialization provides greater aggregate acceleration than nearest-condition restarts using the same solution library. Resolution invariance enables direct deployment of coarse-mesh models on finer meshes without retraining, solution interpolation or target-condition coarse solves. Including data generation and training, estimated campaign speed-ups reach $2.1$-$2.3\times$. No warm run diverges; fewer than $2\%$ fail to satisfy the cold-reference convergence criterion. These results support learned initialization for repeated aerodynamic analyses, while highlighting initialization sensitivity near separation as a remaining limitation.

papers.title: The Lorentz Threshold in Fourier Restriction
papers.authors: R. Shahmurov; V. Shahmurov
papers.abstract: Classical Stein--Tomas restriction controls a Fourier transform on a curved surface, but the estimate changes when its values lie in a Banach space. We determine the sharp Lorentz threshold at the critical exponent $4/3$: for coefficients in $\ell_D^{4/3,q}$, the optimal Gaussian restriction constant grows like $(1+\log D)^{|3/4-1/q|}$. A multiscale wave-packet construction proves sharpness, including the delicate index $q=2$. The same threshold holds for fractional Gaussian noise, while Gaussian type and cotype alone do not distinguish the positive and negative cases. As a dispersive consequence, we establish a sharp Lorentz-channel spacetime estimate for linear capillary waves.

papers.title: Optimal Conversion from Zero-Concentrated to Gaussian Differential Privacy
papers.authors: Yu-Wei Chen; Aaradhya Pandey; Jordan Awan
papers.abstract: Gaussian differential privacy (GDP) and zero-concentrated differential privacy (zCDP) are two competing privacy accounting frameworks, but they share similar minimax lower bounds in various estimation problems. Moreover, it is known that a mechanism satisfying $μ$-GDP satisfies $(μ^2/2)$-zCDP, whereas the converse fails to hold at the same calibration. In this paper, we establish the optimal reverse conversion, showing that every $ρ$-zCDP mechanism satisfies $μ_{\mathrm{zCDP}}(ρ)$-GDP, where $μ_{\mathrm{zCDP}}(ρ)=2Φ^{-1}((1+e^{-t_ρ})^{-1})$ and $t_ρ$ uniquely solves the equation $ρ=t_ρ\tanh(t_ρ/2)$. We also obtain simplified bounds $\sqrt{πρ}\leqμ_{\mathrm{zCDP}}(ρ)\leq\sqrt{8ρ}$, with sharp constants, which imply equivalence of the two frameworks up to constants. This explains why their minimax risks agree up to a constant rescaling of the privacy budget. We show that the squared conversion is strictly convex, which implies that converting zCDP to GDP before applying composition or group privacy yields a tighter GDP guarantee than converting afterward. We also derive the sharp conversion from bounded-range and logistic DP mechanisms (e.g., exponential mechanism) to GDP, where converting before composition but after group privacy gives the tighter guarantee.

papers.title: Geodesics and intrinsic statistics of isolated connections in Hermitian positive-definite matrices
papers.authors: Ronald García Reyes; Pedro Antonio Valdés-Sosa
papers.abstract: Quantifying change in a single covariance, coherence or spectral connection requires a distance that respects the positive-definiteness constraint and holds the surrounding entries fixed. We characterize the Riemannian geometry induced by the affine-invariant metric when one conjugate off-diagonal pair of a Hermitian positive-definite matrix varies under this constraint. A fixed Schur congruence maps the admissible set to an open complex disk and reduces its metric to a two-dimensional form independent of the ambient matrix dimension. The disk is complete, with Gaussian curvature in $(-1/4,0]$, and has unique minimizing geodesics and globally defined logarithms. Its intrinsic distance strictly exceeds the ambient affine-invariant distance between distinct points. Conservation of angular momentum reduces the geodesic boundary-value problem to a single scalar equation with elementary angular and length integrals, enabling distance and logarithm evaluation without shooting. For a declared reference distribution with a finite second intrinsic moment, we establish a unique Fréchet centre and consistency of its empirical estimate, together with a sandwich central limit theorem under the stated regularity conditions. Tangent covariance standardization yields moment identities, and exchangeable rank calibration supplies finite-sample score guarantees. These results provide a geometric and statistical framework for isolated connections on a fixed complement, with explicit limits on extension to varying complements.

papers.title: Optical Magnetic-Field Gating of Photon Avalanching Quantum Processes
papers.authors: Benoît Reynier; Filippo Calavaro; Natalie Fardian-Melamed; Eric Charron; Bleuenn Belz et al.
papers.abstract: Highly nonlinear phenomena, where macroscopic changes are triggered by microscopic perturbations, are ubiquitous in complex systems ranging from epidemic spreading to neural networks. In optics, photon avalanching represents a prime manifestation of such highly nonlinear behavior, characterized by a steep nonlinear response (s) following an avalanche threshold. However, this nonlinearity is typically determined by material composition, making this behavior challenging to tune for adaptive sensing, imaging, and neuromorphic applications. Here, we demonstrate giant optical magnetic field gated threshold and nonlinearity in lanthanide doped nanoparticles. We exploit the distinct quantum selection rules of the avalanche process: while the energy looping cycles of excited state absorption and cross relaxation are primarily electrically driven, the seed excitation, ground state absorption, is a mixed transition permitting magnetic dipole interaction. By positioning the emitters within an optical standing wave to spatially partition the electromagnetic field, we tune the local magnetic to electric field balance to selectively regulate the seeding and amplification probabilities. This allows us to demonstrate an unprecedented dynamic range of control over the power threshold and nonlinearity, tuning the order from s = 15 to s = 62. Furthermore, we harness this spatial separation of electric and magnetic fields using tightly focused cylindrical vector beams to locally sculpt the nonlinearity of a single nanocluster, achieving sub wavelength super resolution imaging that substantially surpasses conventional photon avalanche imaging under Gaussian illumination. These findings establish the magnetic component of light as a practical knob to actively program nonlinear optical dynamics, sub diffraction nanoscopy, and critical quantum dynamics at the nanoscale.

papers.title: SHield: Watermarking 4D Gaussian Splatting via Spherical Harmonic Coefficient Perturbation
papers.authors: Kunal Bhosikar; Prajas Wadekar; Venkata Sai Pranav Bachina; Ankit Gangwal; Charu Sharma et al.
papers.abstract: 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) models are computationally expensive to train but distributed as easily copied parameter files. Existing watermarks protect these assets by fine-tuning the scene against a neural decoder to extract bit strings from rendered video, a heavy process vulnerable to the temporal dynamics of dynamic scenes. However, if the threat model targets the redistributed file itself, verification can be vastly simplified. Because the canonical Spherical-Harmonic (SH) coefficients of 4DGS are time- and view-invariant, parameter-space perturbations can be recovered via deterministic arithmetic. We propose **SHield**, the first non-blind, decoder-free watermarking approach that natively embeds full-resolution RGB images into 4DGS files. SHield tiles a zero-mean payload across the SH coefficients of a key-selected Gaussian subset, applying a brief anchored optimization to preserve visual fidelity. To verify ownership, it geometrically re-associates the key using canonical Gaussian centres to survive file tampering and recovers the payload in closed form. Across 30 scenes (D-NeRF, HyperNeRF, DyNeRF), SHield guarantees near-perfect payload recovery (Pearson $r \geq 0.991$) on all 150 tested models with a mean rendering penalty of $\leq 0.13$~dB. Held-out evaluation yields perfect detection on 400 true trials and zero false positives across $1{,}600$ wrong-subset null trials. We also strictly bound the method's robustness: SHield survives INT8 quantization and $30\%$ opacity pruning for the image payload, and on aggressive SH-degree-1 truncation bit payloads are still decodable.

papers.title: Lower Bounds on Inference Complexity for Polyak-Ruppert Averaged Stochastic Gradient Descent
papers.authors: Denis Belomestny; Alexey Naumov; Sergey Samsonov
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp lower bounds for Gaussian approximation of Polyak-Ruppert averaged stochastic gradient descent with polynomially decreasing step sizes. For every fixed exponent $γ\in(1/2,1)$, a single one-dimensional smooth, strongly convex example has approximation error with the limiting variance of order $n^{1/2-γ}+n^{γ-1}$ in Kolmogorov and convex distances. This matches the existing upper bound throughout the range of $γ$. The nonlinear bias contributes $n^{1/2-γ}$ even when the Gaussian reference uses the finite linearized variance. We also derive a lower bound of order $n^{-(1-γ)/2}$ for the relative mean error of estimating the limiting variance from one SGD trajectory, uniformly over a scalar quadratic family. With the limiting variance known, achieving approximation error $\varepsilon$ on this example takes order $\varepsilon^{-4}$ iterations for the best choice $γ=3/4$. Achieving both Gaussian approximation and relative mean variance-estimation errors at most $\varepsilon$ uniformly over the model class requires at least order $\varepsilon^{-6}$ iterations for every fixed $γ$.

papers.title: Side-Channel Attack Prevention for Post Quantum Cryptography Algorithms: A 3D-Shield Approach
papers.authors: Carl Benda; Eren Kurshan; Aydin Aysu; Paul Franzon
papers.abstract: Despite their theoretical quantum attack resistance, practical implementations of post-quantum cryptography (PQC) algorithms remain susceptible to side-channel attacks. This includes all standard algorithms selected the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) such as Kyber/ML-KEM, Dilithium/ML-DSA, Falcon/FN-DSA and SPHINCS+/SLH-DSA. This paper proposes an alternative defense for side-channel resilience based on 3D integration that uses 3D hardware to shield the underlying cryptographic activity by introducing decoy keys and physical shielding through stacking. The proposed approach can complement other security measures (such as masking and shuffling) on protecting Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) that move computation to dedicated NTT chips. We outline the construction of our approach and validate the effectiveness on a generic attack targeting intermediate computation inside an NTT butterfly.

papers.title: Selective inference for pruned interaction trees with known unequal variances in randomized trials
papers.authors: Tomoshige Nakamura
papers.abstract: Interaction trees reuse outcomes to discover treatment-effect heterogeneity, complicating inference after growth and pruning. We develop selective inference for generalized least-squares (GLS) interaction trees with a common covariate basis and known unequal variances. Under a conditional Gaussian model with positive diagonal covariance, weighted orthogonality reduces survival under additive fixed-penalty pruning to one quadratic inequality supplementing the growth event. This yields exact finite-sample conditional tests and confidence intervals, with retained-path and complete-tree inference agreeing on compatible sections. Under causal identification and a correct reference prognosis, the pruning-invariant GLS target is a signed finite-design weighted contrast of conditional average treatment effects. Simulations at $n=100,200,400,800$ and maximum depths one to three search all adjacent-observation midpoints, support calibration and demonstrate over-rejection when pruning survival is omitted. Compared with a 50:50 honest procedure, full-data learning improves reference-split recovery in some small-sample settings. Root-level median intervals can be shorter, while deep-node intervals and upper tails can be much wider; these comparisons concern each procedure's selected targets. Estimating a common scale with the variance ratio fixed produces modest changes in Selective coverage in the settings examined, without extending the exact guarantee. An exploratory ACTG 175 analysis provides a working-model illustration with estimated arm variances.

papers.title: Extended Onsager's variational principle for nonlinear chemical reaction kinetics in active matter
papers.authors: Xinpeng Xu; Changhao Li; Zhongqiang Xiong; Bin Zheng; Kento Yasuda et al.
papers.abstract: Onsager's variational principle (OVP) constructs dissipative dynamics from free energy, dissipation, and input power, but deterministic rate laws alone do not identify fluctuations or chemical fuel consumption. We examine these distinctions for nonlinear reaction kinetics in active matter. Comparing Gaussian diffusion and Poisson reaction events clarifies when statistical fluctuations match a physical Rayleighian: the reaction dissipation potential must be consistent with counting statistics, local detailed balance links rate bias to chemical affinity, and kinetic scales remain constitutive inputs. Under these conditions, the normalized Rayleighian excess gives the leading rate-fluctuation cost in the frozen-state, many-event regime. Three models illustrate the consequences. Spatially uniform reactions exhibit protocol-dependent nonreciprocal response compatible with fixed-state OVP; different Rayleighian representations can select the same rate without specifying the same fluctuations. In an active emulsion, a finite fuel pool accounts for free-energy transfer and dissolution of a chemically maintained domain after replenishment stops. In a membrane-cytosol model, distinct reaction-channel realizations yield identical protein-density trajectories but different chemical input power. Under a separate kinetic assumption, an exact total-density equation still requires an initial rate and does not determine chemical work or fluctuations. These results clarify the physical and statistical inputs required for constructing reaction-transport models and interpreting their fluctuations.

papers.title: Direct imaging of the Ni $e_g$ hole orbitals in the bilayer nickelate La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_7$
papers.authors: Ethan Saïman; Feiyu Li; Junjie Zhang; Jean-Pascal Rueff; Victor Balédent
papers.abstract: Models of unconventional superconductivity in cuprates and nickelates depend sensitively on the distribution of valence electrons among the $d$ orbitals. But accurately determining the orbital electron or hole occupations in these systems remains a difficult and unresolved task. Here, using $s$-core-level non-resonant inelastic x-ray scattering at the Ni $M_1$ edge, we determine the angular distribution of the Ni $3d$ holes in a single crystal of La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_7$. Our results demonstrate that the hole occupation ratio $\hz/\hx = 0.94\pm0.06$, thus significantly above the expected value of $2/3$ for a filled $d_{z^2}$ orbitals models and close to value expected in a Hund's-coupling picture. Our results support superconductivity scenarios in which both $e_g$ orbitals contribute to the electron-pairing mechanism in La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_7$.

papers.title: Auriga Technical Report: A Task-Agnostic Agent Harness for Zero-Shot Embodied Manipulation
papers.authors: Chengcheng Wang; Yuheng Shi; Siyu Xu; Yutong Wang; Jinjing Zhao et al.
papers.abstract: Vision-language models can interpret instructions and plan manipulation tasks, yet struggle when acting directly as robot policies. On RoboDojo, a large planning-execution gap separates high-level task decisions from physical execution: removing arm execution raises GPT-6 Astra's success rate from 22.5% under the reference control interface to 76.2%. We present Auriga, a task-agnostic agent harness that closes 68.3% of this gap in zero-shot manipulation without target-task trials or resets. In Auriga, the model makes all task decisions over an explicit task belief and acts through either direct tool calls or synthesized multi-step Python programs, while the harness supplies calibrated 3D measurements, finger-referenced dual-arm control, and a single admission gateway to the robot. Before motion, the model inspects a visual trajectory preview while simulation is paused; during execution, the harness checks declared stage tolerances and grasp bounds, stopping the robot on divergence and returning the measured discrepancy for in-place recovery. Developed across 13 cross-task capability iterations and frozen for evaluation, Auriga ranks first on the RoboDojo leaderboard with a 57.7% success rate (64.0 Score), more than doubling the reference harness on the same model, and remains first under scene randomization while learned policies drop by up to 33.9%. On RoboCasa365, the same frozen harness reaches a 73.2% success rate, outperforming VLA-assisted agents by up to 23.1% on composite tasks.   Project page: https://auriga.stelledge.com/ Code: https://github.com/lose4578/Auriga

papers.title: Semiclassical Wave Packet Dynamics For Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations with Harmonic Potentials
papers.authors: Jared Smith; Tomoki Ohsawa
papers.abstract: We propose an approximate Hamiltonian dynamics for the Gross--Pitaevskii equation $i\hbarψ_t = -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}Δψ+ V(x)ψ+ \hbar^2 λ|ψ|^2ψ$ with harmonic potential $V(x)$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. We do this by extending the Gaussian ansatz of Perez-Garcia et al.~(Phys.~Rev.~A 56, 1424 (1997)) to the semiclassical wave packets of Hagedorn. We derive the evolution equations for the wave packets from the Hamiltonian/symplectic perspective, rather than the Lagrangian/variational one taken by Perez-Garcia et al. We first show that these two perspectives yield identical evolution equations in the Gaussian case. We then derive the evolution equations for an arbitrary element of the semiclassical wave packets. Finally, we demonstrate the efficacy of the approximate dynamics with numerical experiments.

papers.title: From Gaussian to stable and back: Non-Pareto points in growing dimension
papers.authors: Chinmoy Bhattacharjee; Andrii Ilienko; Bochen Jin; Ilya Molchanov
papers.abstract: We study the number of non-Pareto points in two high-dimensional models: a homogeneous Poisson point process and a fixed-size sample of independent uniform points in the unit cube. A point is non-Pareto if some other sample point is coordinatewise less than or equal to it. As the dimension grows on the logarithmic scale of the intensity or sample size, the asymptotic behavior exhibits a surprising sequence of transitions: from Gaussian to stable fluctuations, back to Gaussian, then to a Poisson limit at the sparsity threshold, followed by the eventual disappearance of non-Pareto points.   We identify the critical thresholds, normalizations, and limiting laws in both models. Notably, the return to Gaussianity occurs while the stability index remains strictly below $2$ and is driven by a change in the dominant fluctuation mechanism. Moreover, in part of the returning Gaussian regime, the natural normalization is the square root of the expected count rather than its standard deviation. At the stable--Gaussian transition, the two mechanisms can coexist, giving rise to a sum of independent stable and Gaussian random variables.

papers.title: Pop Goes the Verifier: Phoneme-Targeted Data Poisoning of Voice Liveness Detection
papers.authors: Eshaq Jamdar; Amith Kamath Belman
papers.abstract: Many Automated Speaker Verification Systems (ASVs) commonly employ liveliness detection techniques, such as VoicePop, which identify genuine speech by analyzing low- frequency pop bursts from plosive phonemes using Gammatone Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (GFCC) and an SVM classifier. While effective against traditional replay attacks, such systems are vulnerable to data poisoning techniques. Prior work shows that broadly applied SyntheticPop attacks can collapse model to accuracy to as low as 14.01% using only 20% poisoned samples, but the resulting artifacts are easily detectable when visualizing the waveform energies. This paper introduces Pop Goes the Verifier, a stealthier phoneme injection poisoning attack. By leveraging FastSpeech 2 (FS2) with a modified HiFi-GAN vocoder, we inject localized pop bursts at plosive phoneme locations and overlay subtle Gaussian noise to reduce the visibility of injected artifacts in waveform and spectrogram analysis. Using the ASVSpoof 2019 as the dataset, we observe that the approach achieves a moderate poisoning attack while providing greater resistance to signal-level inspection than the original SyntheticPop attack.

papers.title: QVR3D: Query-Guided Visual Reasoning for Training-Free 3D Grounding
papers.authors: Jung-Hao Kao; Jing-En Huang; Jia-Wei Liao; Tzuhsuan Huang; Yu-Lun Liu et al.
papers.abstract: 3D visual grounding localizes objects in 3D scenes from natural language descriptions, requiring reasoning over semantics, spatial relationships, and multi-view observations. Training-free approaches avoid costly annotations but often rely on explicit scene transformation or scene-level frame selection, which may waste limited visual capacity on query-irrelevant regions. We observe that effective grounding should prioritize observations that provide evidence for the query rather than uniformly represent the entire scene. Based on this insight, we introduce QVR3D, a query-guided visual reasoning framework that operates on RGB-D observations using off-the-shelf foundation models. QVR3D combines Query-Guided Maximum Coverage (QGMC) for selecting complementary query-relevant views with Grounding Probability Estimation (GPE) that integrates instance confidence, attribute consistency, and relationship consistency. The framework supports both single- and multi-object grounding without task-specific adaptation. Experiments on ScanRefer and Nr3D achieve state-of-the-art zero-shot performance, while QGMC also improves frame efficiency across multiple 3D vision-language tasks. Our code is available at https://github.com/jwliao1209/QVR3D.

papers.title: Rogue waves in the dam-break problem for the Kundu--Eckhaus equation
papers.authors: Jiaming Sun; Zhen Wang; Tianwei Qiu
papers.abstract: We study rogue wave formation in the dam-break problem for the Kundu--Eckhaus equation with deterministic and randomly perturbed box initial data. For the unperturbed real box, the gauge transformation and Galilean invariance relate the intensity evolution to that of the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation. The Kundu--Eckhaus parameter determines the phase, the real shift of the discrete spectrum and the drift velocity. We compare uniform, Gaussian and Laplace perturbations with equal variance and the same correlation scale in the underlying Gaussian field. At the larger perturbation strengths considered, the Laplace perturbations yield larger mean maximum intensities and higher exceedance probabilities for the normalized intensity at the final simulation time, but smaller amplification relative to the initial maximum intensity.

papers.title: Entropy-Regularized Reinforcement Learning for the Regime-Switching Consumption-Investment Problem
papers.authors: Congde Hu; Danping Li; Xun Li; Yijie Zeng
papers.abstract: This paper establishes an entropy-regularized reinforcement learning (ERRL) framework for the continuous-time consumption-investment problem under a regime-switching market model with general utility functions. By incorporating randomized exploratory policies and Shannon entropy regularization into the stochastic optimal control formulation, we derive closed-form representations for the optimal exploratory consumption and investment strategies. Specifically, the optimal investment strategy follows a multivariate Gaussian distribution, whereas the optimal consumption strategy takes the form of a Gibbs measure---which specializes to a Gamma distribution under logarithmic utility and a non-standard exponential distribution under power utility. Crucially, our theoretical analysis reveals that the classical deterministic optimal decisions correspond to the mode---rather than the mean---of these exploratory distributions. Furthermore, we establish the convergence of the exploratory value function to its classical unregularized counterpart as the temperature parameter vanishes. For algorithmic design, we develop a continuous-time q-learning framework grounded in a novel continuous-time q-function, prove the policy improvement theorem, and establish martingale characterizations for both on-policy and off-policy learning. We find that parameterizing the actor network based on theoretical distribution families can help accelerate convergence and enhance numerical stability. Furthermore, numerical experiments across regime-switching environments provide empirical support for our theoretical findings, demonstrating stable loss convergence as well as the monotonicity and concavity of the learned value functions.

papers.title: Alternative Tikhonov-Type Regularization for the Calderón Inverse Conductivity Problem
papers.authors: Pavel B. Dubovski; Charles Morehead
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the application of two regularization methods, classical Tikhonov and Alternative Tikhonov regularization, to the Calderón inverse conductivity problem. We develop an iterative reconstruction scheme based on linearizing the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map and approximating conductivity updates using Gaussian basis functions. The resulting linear systems are solved using both regularization methods, with particular attention given to the derivation and numerical implementation of Alternative Tikhonov regularization. We compare the performance of these methods through numerical experiments on a synthetic conductivity containing two localized regions of differing conductivity. A total of 666 reconstruction tests are performed across varying regularization parameters, damping factors, and iteration counts. The lowest relative reconstruction errors obtained are 0.064730 for Alternative Tikhonov and 0.065173 for classical Tikhonov regularization. Although both methods produce comparable reconstructions, Alternative Tikhonov achieves the lowest observed error. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of both approaches within the proposed reconstruction scheme and motivate further investigation into parameter selection, numerical stability, and reconstruction accuracy.

papers.title: Active Jarzynski and Crooks Relations for Driven Jump-Diffusions
papers.authors: Shuyuan Fan; Bing Miao; Jinqiao Duan; Qi Zhang
papers.abstract: Non-conservative active driving breaks detailed balance in non-Gaussian jump-diffusions, obscuring the connection between external protocol work, housekeeping dissipation, and free-energy differences. Here, we establish exact finite-time fluctuation relations for driven Markov jump-diffusions---encompassing infinite-activity Lévy processes---by comparing path probabilities under the forward and current-reversed dual dynamics relative to the instantaneous steady state (ISS). We derive a trajectory-level decomposition of total entropy production that cleanly separates transient state relaxation, housekeeping heat, and external protocol driving. When the ISS takes a Gibbsian form, gauge-tilting the dual path measure yields an Active Jarzynski equality, $\langle\exp[-(W+Δs_{\mathrm{act}})]\rangle_{π_0}=e^{-ΔF}$, which incorporates active housekeeping entropy $Δs_{\mathrm{act}}$ alongside mechanical work $W$ and coexists with the conventional Jarzynski equality. Under protocol reversal, this dual framework further reveals an Active Crooks relation, where the asymmetry between forward and reverse work distributions is governed by the conditional exponential average of active dissipation. Our results provide a framework for recovering free-energy differences in driven jump-diffusions with Gibbsian instantaneous steady states and for characterizing active irreversibility through trajectory statistics.

papers.title: Equivariant $\mathcal{Z}$-stability for amenable actions
papers.authors: Eusebio Gardella
papers.abstract: We prove that every amenable action of a countable discrete group on a separable, simple, unital, nuclear, $\mathcal{Z}$-stable C*-algebra absorbs the trivial action on $\mathcal{Z}$ up to cocycle conjugacy. The group may be nonamenable, as in Suzuki's recent examples, and no assumptions on outerness or on the tracial state space are needed. This extends OpenAI's result for amenable groups to amenable actions. Amenability of the action cannot be omitted in general, as examples of the author and Lupini show. More generally, we show that every tracially amenable action on a separable, unital, $\mathcal{Z}$-stable C*-algebra with traces admits invariant central copies of all matrix algebras, without simplicity or nuclearity. For amenable actions on simple nuclear algebras, equivariant property (SI) allows one to deduce $\mathcal{Z}$-stability from this. As applications, we obtain absorption of $\mathcal{Z}$ for intermediate subalgebras in the crossed product, and also pure infiniteness for outer amenable actions of nonamenable groups.   The basic techniques involving Gaussian variables originate in OpenAI's preprint, and are also the main new tool in its proposed solution to the Toms--Winter conjecture. We extend these techniques in order to deal with the weight functions coming from amenability, and one of the main new ingredients is the fact that one can replace an amenable action by an auxiliary one for which the amenability weights are central.   In order to make the probabilistic tools accessible to the community beyond what is used here, we include an appendix where the theory is developed assuming only an elementary background, and where the relevant estimates are proved in detail.

papers.title: Stability threshold for 3D Boussinesq equations with rotation near the Couette flow and vertical stratified temperature
papers.authors: Wenting Huang; Zekai Luo; Ying Sun; Jiahong Wu; Xiaojing Xu
papers.abstract: The most important features that distinguish fluid flow in the atmosphere and ocean are the effects of rotation and stratification, which are described by the Boussinesq equations with rotation. This paper examines the stability threshold at high Reynolds number $\mathbf{Re}$ for the 3D Boussinesq equations with rotation near Couette flow and a vertical stratified temperature. For the zero modes, the combined effects of rotation and stratification sustain velocity-temperature oscillations with frequencies bounded away from zero. In the stable rotational regime, rotation suppresses the linear growth associated with the lift-up effect, while stratification sustains oscillations in the double zero modes. Although the zero modes dynamics are not fully dispersive, we exploit the structure of the oscillatory phases and cancellations in the equations to obtain a modified energy estimate for the entire zero modes system. Combining this estimate with enhanced dissipation and inviscid damping of the nonzero modes, we establish a bound for the stability threshold, with order $\mathbf{Re}^{-2/3}(1+\log\mathbf{Re})^{-1-a_0}$ for any fixed $a_0\in(0,1/2)$.

papers.title: PSF-Informed Reconstruction: An Enhanced 2D Directional Filtered Backprojection Method for Cone-Beam Rotary Computed Laminography
papers.authors: Chengxiang Wang; Wei Yu; Baodong Liu
papers.abstract: Cone-beam rotary computed laminography (CL) presents a viable alternative to cone-beam CT for imaging objects with high aspect ratios. Conventional reconstruction techniques, such as CL-FBP and CL-FDK, often yield suboptimal results charac?terized by pronounced superimposition artifacts, reduced contrast,and blurred edges, primarily due to their reliance on 1D row-wise filtering along detector rows. To address these limitations and improve reconstruction quality, we proposed a novel 2D directional filtered backprojection (DFBP) method based on the point spread function (PSF). First, an exact expression for the projection process is derived by establishing the relationship between a reconstructed pixel and its corresponding projection point on the detector. Second, a revised backprojection process incorporating two weighting factors is introduced to counteract the nonlinearity inherent in conventional backprojection, leading to a simplified PSF formulation. Third, to circumvent the computational burden of 3D image space filtering,an approximate method by linearizing the coordinate relationship in Fourier space under some assumptions is developed that transfers the 3D filtering operation to the 2D projection space. This approach facilitates the derivation of a formally simple yet effective 2D direc?tional filter, which integrates a 2D von Hann window and a 2D sinc window. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method produces reconstructions with superior contrast, sharper boundaries,and fewer superimposition artifacts compared to CL-FBP and CL?FDK. Moreover, it enables more accurate recovery of internal structures, such as bubble defects and electronic components.

papers.title: Gravitational form factors of heavy quarkonia and their nonrelativistic expansion in a self-consistent light-front quark model
papers.authors: Ho-Meoyng Choi; Chueng-Ryong Ji; Hyeon-Dong Son
papers.abstract: We investigate the gravitational form factors of the pseudoscalar heavy quarkonia $η_c(1S,2S)$ and $η_b(1S,2S)$ in a light-front quark model with physical radial wave functions represented by orthogonal mixtures of the two lowest harmonic-oscillator basis states $φ_{1S}$ and $φ_{2S}$. The Bakamjian--Thomas prescription is applied consistently to constituent matrix elements and Lorentz prefactors at the integrand level. Working in the $Δ^+=0$ frame with $Δ=P'-P$ and $t=Δ^2$, we extract $A_q(t)$ from the quark energy--momentum tensor components $T_q^{++}$, $T_q^{+i}$, and $T_q^{ij}$, and $D_q(t)$ from $T_q^{+-}$, $T_q^{-i}$, and $T_q^{ii}$ using appropriate momentum-transfer projections. The independent extractions agree in the full relativistic calculation and in the analytic nonrelativistic expansions through $ O(v^2)$, where $v=β/m_Q$, $β$ is the Gaussian width, and $m_Q$ is the constituent mass. At zero momentum transfer, the expansions give $D_q^{φ_{1S}}(0)=-v^2+ O(v^4)$ and $D_q^{φ_{2S}}(0)=-2/3-(13/3)v^2+O(v^4)$. The interference, defined as the sum of the two cross overlaps, first contributes as $D_q^{\mathrm{cross}}(0)=-(4/\sqrt{6})v^2+O(v^4)$. Thus, the pure Gaussian $1S$ contribution is suppressed, whereas a nonzero $2S$ admixture at fixed mixing angle leaves an $O(v^0)$ D-term in the physical ground state. Full numerical results for the mixed states illustrate the effects of heavy-quark flavor and radial structure on mass distributions and internal stresses.

papers.title: MarkovTS: Pretrained State-Transition Representations for Zero-Shot Time Series Generation
papers.authors: Yujie Li; Zezhi Shao; Jingbo Zhou; Yongjun Xu; Xueqi Cheng et al.
papers.abstract: Across heterogeneous real-world domains, time-series generation supports simulation, model development, and data augmentation by generating sequences that preserve target-domain statistics and temporal dependencies when real observations are scarce or costly. However, existing methods predominantly address in-domain generation, limiting their reuse in unseen domains. We study reference-conditioned zero-shot time series generation: target domains are unseen during pretraining, generation uses a single target-domain reference sequence, and no model parameters are updated. MarkovTS characterizes sequence evolution through local morphologies and their ordered transitions at multiple temporal scales. Its pretrained encoder quantizes normalized time-series patches into multiscale morphological states with a state codebook, while a transition codebook encodes contextual transitions between adjacent intervals. These transferable state-transition representations condition a pretrained flow-matching model. At generation, the frozen model combines a reference-derived condition with independent Gaussian noise to produce stochastic samples that retain the reference's temporal organization. Across 12 unseen target datasets, MarkovTS outperforms strong baselines in most distributional comparisons and generates diverse, reference-consistent sequences. As downstream augmentation, its samples yield overall gains across forecasting, classification, and anomaly detection benchmarks and diverse model families. Our code is available at https://github.com/blisky-li/MarkovTS.

papers.title: A Bayesian Magnitude-Composition Model for Tree-Size Distributions and Stand-Tables
papers.authors: Andrew O. Finley; Malcolm S. Itter; Arthur Spitta; Arne Nothdurft
papers.abstract: Sparse forest inventories often provide too few plots to estimate species-specific tree-size distributions for individual stands. We develop a general Bayesian magnitude-composition model that separates overall abundance from its allocation among categories. A negative-binomial model describes total counts, while multinomial models describe how those counts are allocated among categories. In forest inventory, this construction allocates trees among species and then size classes within species, without imposing a parametric form on the tree-size distribution. Covariates inform both abundance and composition. Shared latent factors represent residual spatial and group-level dependence among categories using relatively few processes, while smoothing priors on regression coefficients borrow information across neighboring size classes. Nearest-neighbor Gaussian processes support efficient spatial computation. Joint posterior prediction and area-weighted aggregation yield stand-tables---tree densities by species and size class---and derived measures such as size-class diversity, with associated uncertainty. Simulations show small estimation errors and near-nominal predictive-interval coverage for forest and stand summaries. An application combining field plots and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) covariates illustrates estimation of species-specific distributions of diameter at breast height and size-class diversity in sampled and unsampled stands.

papers.title: Closed-Form Gaussian Mixture Representations of d-Dimensional Triangulated Domains
papers.authors: Ali Darijani; Benedikt Stratmann; Uwe D. Hanebeck; Ratan Bahadur Thapa; Jürgen Beyerer et al.
papers.abstract: We derive a Gaussian Mixture (GM) representation of a full-dimensional subset of Euclidean space with finite volume from a finite simplicial triangulation in closed form.
